title: Deacons
hookLine: since 1967 permanent deacons, often married, serve in the Latin Church

lines: A STOLE WORN LIKE A SASH.
HIS WIFE IN THE THIRD PEW.
cards: Sunday morning. A man in an alb steps up to the ambo to proclaim the Gospel. His stole doesn't hang straight down like the priest's: it crosses his chest from one shoulder to the opposite hip, like a sash.
He reads, then preaches, and somewhere in the homily mentions his grandson's soccer game. In the third pew, his wife rolls her eyes and smiles.
On Monday he's back at his job; on Thursday evening, at the county jail, leading a Bible study. He is ordained, and married, and neither a priest nor on his way to becoming one. Today, deacons.

teach.b: A deacon is a servant. The Catechism calls Christ himself the deacon, or servant, of all.
In Mark's Gospel, Jesus says it of himself, in the Douay-Rheims: "For the Son of man also is not come to be ministered unto: but to minister, and to give his life a redemption for many."
To minister there means to serve, to wait on.

teach.h: SEVEN CHOSEN TO SERVE THE WIDOWS.
teach.b: Back on day five hundred forty-one, you met the seven in Acts: Greek-speaking widows overlooked in the daily food, and seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom, chosen by the community, with the apostles laying hands on them.
Stephen was one. Tradition sees in them the first deacons. By the time Paul writes to Philippi, he greets the church "with the bishops and deacons."

The Catechism lists it: assisting the bishop and priests at the Eucharist, giving communion, witnessing and blessing marriages, proclaiming the Gospel and preaching, presiding at funerals, and giving himself to works of charity.
He does not consecrate the Eucharist or hear confessions. He is ordained, the Catechism says, not for priesthood but for service. And there are two kinds.
Men on the road to priesthood are ordained deacons first.
But the Second Vatican Council asked that the diaconate be restored in the Latin Church as a permanent rank, open to men of mature age, including married men.

teach.h: NOT TO BE MINISTERED UNTO, BUT TO MINISTER.
teach.b: So the deacon at the ambo is something old and something renewed at once: a married man, ordained to serve.

how: Catholic deacons are ordained by a bishop. At Mass they proclaim the Gospel, may preach, and assist at the altar; they also baptize, witness marriages, lead funeral rites and serve in works of charity. In the Latin Church, permanent deacons may be married men who keep their jobs and families.

games.q: you're one of the apostles in Jerusalem. the Greek-speaking widows are being overlooked in the daily food. what do you do?
o: stop preaching and run the food lines yourselves.
ask the community to choose seven men full of the Spirit, and lay hands on them for the work.
tell the widows to find another community.
games.why: the apostles had the community choose seven, Stephen among them, and laid hands on them. tradition sees in them the first deacons.

practice: Bring to mind a deacon you've seen at a baptism, a funeral or a Sunday Mass, or, if you don't know one, anyone whose work is to serve quietly: a nurse's aide, a cafeteria worker, a food-pantry volunteer.
Picture their hands at work. If you pray, thank God for them and ask strength for their service; if you don't, simply wish them a good day's work.

wordCard.voice: Deacons. Men ordained not for priesthood but for service: to proclaim the Gospel, assist at the altar and serve in charity, and in the Latin Church today, including married men. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek, a servant: the Catechism calls Christ the 'deacon' or servant of all.

carryVoice: Your line: servants. Ordained not to be ministered unto, but to minister. See you tomorrow.
